source.title: Omni-Safety under Cross-Modality Conflict: Vulnerabilities, Dynamics Mechanisms and Efficient Alignment
source.authors: Kun Wang; Zhe-Rui Li; Zhe-Xu Zhou; Yi-Tong Zhang; Yan Mi; Kun Yang; Yimei Zhang; Junhao Dong; Zhong-Xiang Sun; Qian-Kun Li; Yang Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study measures difference-in-means refusal vectors and their geometry across modalities, and tests adding refusal vectors as steering interventions. It does not perform the original all-layer, all-position ablation.
record.gate_note: The study also evaluates cross-modal refusal rates, but those results alone do not test whether attacks suppress the direction (V3). The mean activations used to construct vectors are part of the method, not separate outcome rows. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study extracts the difference-in-means (harmful minus benign) refusal direction in omni-modal models and measures how it carries from text to image, audio, video and cross-modal inputs, on Qwen2.5-Omni-7B. It also adds the direction at layers 15-17 and reports refusal rates on harmful and benign inputs (Table 2). This is a new setting (modalities) using the original's direction and addition. No ablation or weight edit is performed. The OmniSteer results (Table 3) are the study's own trained-adapter method compared with baselines, so they are method performance, not a test of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that cross-modal inputs reduce refusal through 'Mid-layer Dissolution' driven mainly by shrinking refusal-vector magnitude, not direction. They find a modality-invariant pure refusal direction, and propose OmniSteer, adaptive steering with an SVD golden vector, which raises RSR from 69.9% to 91.2% while preserving benign acceptance and OmniBench accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the difference-in-means refusal-vector definition and activation addition, but extracts a shared SVD direction and applies it at selected layers (including adaptive layerwise steering), rather than ablating the direction at every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by modality and steering strength; the paper reports reduced cross-modal vector magnitude and tests steering at Layers 15 to 17 with alpha values 0.02, 0.05, and 0.1. The reported benign acceptance differs substantially at alpha 0.1.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal vectors from 7 modality combinations lie mostly in a 2-D subspace. PC1 (80.3%) is read as refusal intensity and PC2 as a modality-bias axis (sequential vs spatial inputs); an SVD 'golden' vector shared across modalities is extracted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Modality-specific refusal vectors share one refusal direction plus a modality-bias offset, rather than forming distinct refusal directions.

record.problems: The central mechanistic analysis is on Qwen2.5-Omni-7B only. There is no all-layer ablation test. The benign acceptance rate under strong static steering is low, and reported run averages have no error bars or other uncertainty estimates. Some table results are difficult to assign model-by-model from the flattened text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 contains per-model and per-dataset results, but the flattened layout does not reliably map every value to its model and metric. The record uses only aggregate outcomes explicitly summarized in the text, plus the OmniBench summary; no ambiguous table cells were assigned.

untested.parts: Ablating or projecting out the direction to remove refusal; capability preservation under ablation; models other than Qwen2.5-Omni-7B for the static steering test.
Transfer across languages, across model variants, and from base to instruct models. Only transfer across input modalities within one model is tested.
No test of affine, cone or multi-direction accounts of refusal itself; the PCA concerns modality-bias offsets.
No test that attacks suppress the direction; cross-modal inputs reduce the projection, but adversarial robustness training against ablation is absent.

missing.what: Per-modality and per-alpha RSR/BAR for text, mean and SVD vectors, including alpha 0.05 (BAR about 74-82%) and alpha 0.02 (RSR about 86-98%, BAR about 86-96%), with vanilla baselines
Static SVD steering at alpha 0.2 without adapter: RSR 97.0/84.6/99.6 but BAR drops to 48.2 (BeaverTails) and 63.2 (HoliSafe)
Dependence on target layer (4-6 vs 15-17 vs 23-25) of refusal induced by steering

record.verdict_notes: V4 links on R1-R15 were removed: the 'others' in this study are modality-bias offsets, not additional refusal directions, and the paper itself argues for one shared refusal direction. The reader framed low benign acceptance under alpha 0.1 steering as a capability limit. Relative to V1 it is evidence that adding the direction induces refusal on harmless inputs. Mechanistic analyses use only Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, and no uncertainty is reported. The text says PC2 explains 15.3% in panel (b) and 9.5% in panel (a).

versions.untested_parts: No ablation or removal experiment; no test projecting the direction out of every layer and position. Harmless-request acceptance is evaluated under limited steering settings rather than demonstrating refusal of all harmless requests.
No test that attacks work by suppressing the refusal direction, or that training against its ablation improves robustness.
The study analyzes modality-specific refusal vectors and a shared direction plus modality biases, but does not compare affine, cone, or other alternatives as behavioral causal mechanisms.
No experiment separates harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
Tests concern modality transfer. It does not test transfer across languages, base-to-instruct models, or whether a vector extracted from one model transfers to another.
No comparison of refusal training methods or training stages.
No evaluation of reasoning models as a class or of whether refusal direction ablation works in them.

tranche.reason: It applies the diff-in-means refusal direction and activation addition in a new setting (omni-modal, cross-modal inputs) and reports refusal rates and transfer measures. It has no ablation and uses an LLM judge, so T1 doesn't fit.

source_check.notes: The text extraction scrambled Table 2. Reading it so the Average column equals the subset mean gives vanilla RSR 78.9/83.7/74.2 and BAR 88.8/98.3/98.4 (T+I/T+A/T+V), averages 78.9 and 95.2. The pack's per-subset vanilla values don't fit this. The mechanistic analyses use one model with no system prompt, an LLM judge (Qwen3-30B-A3B) and 3-run averages. The 88.3%/9.8% split adds variances of norms and cosines, which are in different units. Counting input modality as a V6 'variant' is a stretch of the wording.

statements.correction: Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, layers 15-17, alpha 0.1, no system prompt. Vanilla RSR: average 78.9, subsets 74.2-83.7. Steered RSR: 99.4-100 on every subset. Vanilla BAR: average 95.2, subsets 88.8-98.4. Steered average BAR: 38.8 (text), 41.1 (mean), 46.2 (SVD). The mean and SVD vectors combine the text, single-modal and cross-modal refusal vectors.
statements.problem: 'Benign acceptance about 97%' is not in the text: vanilla average BAR is 95.2. 'From a vanilla 74.2' quotes the lowest subset only. 'From text/cross-modal data' is loose: the mean and SVD vectors pool every modality's refusal vector.
